title: Thank God for the ache
takeaway: The ability to feel deeply, even when it hurts, is a gift from God.
scene: The poet starts by doing something surprising. Instead of complaining about his pain, he thanks God for it.

original: تڑپ دل دی جگر دا سوز دتا، میں رب دا شکر ہزار کیتا
فیر درد دی دولت عطا کیتی، اپنا کرم کھلا کردگار کیتا
transliteration: Tarap dil di jigar da soz ditta, main Rab da shukar hazaar keeta
Pher dard di daulat ataa keeti, apna karam khulla Kirdgaar keeta
translation: He gave my heart longing and my soul a burning; I thanked God a thousand times.
Then He gave me the treasure of pain; the Creator opened His generosity wide.
couplets.story: God gave him a restless, aching heart, and he thanked God a thousand times for it. Then God gave him something even more precious: the 'treasure' of pain. He sees it as God being generous with him.

original: شوخ رنگ خشبوواں دے حلیاں تھیں وحشت ودھ گئی ہور دیوانیاں دی
ایس خزاں نمانی نے کیہ کرنا ستم جدوں کیتا ہے بہار کیتا
transliteration: Shokh rang khushbuaan de hileyaan thin vehshat vadh gayi hor deewaaniyaan di
Is khizaan nimaani ne ki karna, sitam jadon keeta hai bahaar keeta
translation: The bright colours and scents only made the lovers wilder.
What harm can poor autumn do? Whenever cruelty came, it was spring that did it.
couplets.story: The bright colours and sweet smells of spring made the lovers even crazier. He jokes that autumn isn't the problem. Every time he's been hurt, it was spring, the season of beauty and love, that did it.

original: پیتی ہے پر دوستو قسم لے لیو میں نئیں جام صراحی دے نال پیتی
کسے کھیویاں اکھیاں نال تک کے مینوں مست بے ہوش سرشار کیتا
transliteration: Peeti hai par dosto qasam lai lo, main nahin jaam suraahi de naal peeti
Kise khehviyaan akhiyaan naal tak ke mainu mast be-hosh sarshaar keeta
translation: I have been drinking, friends, but I swear I didn't drink from a cup or a jug.
Someone looked at me with intoxicating eyes, and it left me drunk, senseless and overflowing.
couplets.story: His friends think he's drunk. He admits it, but swears there was no alcohol. Someone just looked at him with amazing eyes, and that look made him feel drunk and dizzy.

original: اوس بت نوں ویکھ کے وچ رنداں جوش تیک وچ واہ سبحان اللہ
پہلاں تسبیحاں توڑیاں زاہداں نے فیر جبیاں نوں تار تار کیتا
transliteration: Os butt nu vekh ke vich rindaan josh teek vich vaah Subhaan Allah
Pehlaan tasbeehaan toriyaan zaahidaan ne, pher jubbiyaan nu taar taar keeta
translation: Seeing that idol, even the free spirits were swept up in passion, crying 'Glory be to God!'
First the strict holy men broke their prayer beads, then they tore their robes to shreds.
couplets.story: When people saw the Beloved, even the carefree crowd cried out 'Subhan Allah!' Even the strict, serious religious men lost control. They broke their prayer beads and ripped their robes.

original: چن ول چکور پرواز کردے شمع ول پرواز پروانیاں دی
بناں پراں توں پونچدے لوک اڈ کے جس تھاویں ڈیرا میرے یار کیتا
transliteration: Chann val chakor parvaaz karde, shamaa val parvaaz parwaaniyaan di
Binaa paraan ton pohnchde lok ud ke jis thaaveen dera mere yaar keeta
translation: Chakor birds fly toward the moon; moths fly toward the candle.
People fly there without wings, wherever my Beloved has made his home.
couplets.story: The chakor bird flies toward the moon. The moth flies toward the candle flame. And people fly too, without wings, to wherever the Beloved is.

original: گئیاں میٹیاں اکھاں تے قبر اتے میرا گل گلشن نو بہار آیا
احمدؔ وانگ نرگس اکھاں کھول کے میں ساری عمر جہدا انتظار کیتا
transliteration: Gaiyaan meetiyaan akhaan te qabar utte mera gul gulshan nau-bahaar aaya
Ahmad vaang nargis akhaan khol ke main saari umar jihda intezaar keeta
translation: My eyes had closed for good when, at my grave, my flower, the fresh spring of my garden, arrived:
the one I waited for my whole life, Ahmad, with eyes wide open like the narcissus.
couplets.story: He waited his whole life for the Beloved to come, eyes always open like a flower watching. They came at last, but only after he died. They finally visited his grave.

deeper:
Thanking God for pain is a classic Sufi idea. A heart that can ache for God is a heart that is alive, so even the longing is a gift (ata). The scene of holy men breaking their prayer beads and tearing their robes is a famous image in this tradition. When someone truly glimpses God's beauty, the outward forms of piety fall away.

The ending, the Beloved arriving at the grave, points to the Sufi belief that the final meeting with God comes at death. The lover's whole life is the waiting.
why: It flips our usual thinking: instead of 'why is this happening to me?', the poet says 'thank you for letting me feel this much'.
prompt: Is there a hard feeling you've had that also taught you something, or made you more alive?
notes: A second version of this ghazal is printed on pages 53–54. It is kept here as a variant, with its two extra couplets, rather than as a separate poem.

variant.summary: The book prints this ghazal a second time on pages 53–54. The wording is slightly different (for example 'my Lord's kindness' instead of 'the Creator'), and it has two couplets that are not on page 28. Those two extra couplets are given here.

original: اینان گوشہ نشینیاں بھلا کتھے ریس کرنی اے اہناں دیوانیاں دی
دس وار تے پئی تے دار اتے جنہاں یار دا جا دیدار کیتا
transliteration: Inaan gosha-nasheeniyaan bhala kitthe rees karni ae ehnaan deewaaniyaan di
Dass vaar te pai te daar utte jinhaan yaar da ja deedaar keeta
translation: How could these recluses ever compete with those madmen,
who went up on the gallows and saw the Beloved there?
extraCouplets.story: People who hide away from the world to be holy can't compete with the 'crazy' lovers. Those lovers climbed the gallows like Mansur and saw the Beloved face to face.

original: رہیا کھولدا گنڈاں کہ نکل جاواں وچ گنجھلاں پئے نہ جان میری
کیتے جتن ہزار نہ بچ سکیا ایسا زلف شب گیر نے وار کیتا
transliteration: Rehiya kholda gandhaan ke nikal jaavaan, vich gunjhlaan pae na jaan meri
Keete jatan hazaar na bach sakiya, aisa zulf-e-shabgeer ne vaar keeta
translation: I kept untying the knots so I could escape, so my life wouldn't get caught in the tangles;
I tried a thousand ways, but couldn't escape: that's how the night-dark tresses struck.
extraCouplets.story: He kept trying to untie the knots and free himself before he got trapped. He tried everything. But the Beloved's long dark hair, as dark as night, caught him anyway.
